questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of c from the Lagrange's mean value theorem for which $f(x)=\sqrt{25-x^{2}}$ in $[1,5]$, is
questions.solution:
It is clear that $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ has a definite and unique value for each $x \in[1,5] .$
Thus, for every point in the interval $[1,5]$, the value of $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ exists.
So, $f(x)$ is continuous in the interval $[1,5]$.
Also, $f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{-x}{\sqrt{25-x^{2}}}$, which clearlyexists
for all $x$ in an open interval $(1,5)$.
So, $\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})$ is differentiable in $(1,5)$.
So, there must be a value $c \in[1,5]$ such that
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{c})=\frac{\mathrm{f}(5)-\mathrm{f}(1)}{5-1}=\frac{0-\sqrt{24}}{4} \\
&=\frac{0-2 \sqrt{6}}{4}=\frac{-\sqrt{6}}{2} \\
& \text { But } \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{c})=\frac{-\mathrm{c}}{\sqrt{25-\mathrm{c}^{2}}} \\
\Rightarrow & \frac{-\mathrm{c}}{\sqrt{25-\mathrm{c}^{2}}}=-\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2} \\
\Rightarrow & 4 \mathrm{c}^{2}=6\left(25-\mathrm{c}^{2}\right) \\
\Rightarrow & 4 \mathrm{c}^{2}=150-6 \mathrm{c}^{2} \Rightarrow 10 \mathrm{c}^{2}=150 \\
\Rightarrow & \mathrm{c}^{2}=15 \Rightarrow \mathrm{c}=\pm \sqrt{15} \\
\therefore & \mathrm{c}=\sqrt{15} \in[1,5]
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The minimum value of $\frac{x}{\log x}$ is
questions.solution:
Let $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\frac{\mathrm{x}}{\log \mathrm{x}}\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=\frac{\log \mathrm{x}-1}{(\log \mathrm{x})^{2}}$
For maxima and minima, put $f^{\prime}(x)=0\log x-1=0\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{e}$
Now, $f^{\prime \prime}(x)=\frac{(\log x)^{2} \cdot \frac{1}{x}-(\log x-1) \cdot \frac{2 \log x}{x}}{(\log x)^{4}}\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{e})=\frac{\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}}-0}{1}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}} \gt 0\therefore \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ is minimum at $\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{e}$.
Hence, minimum value of $f(x)$ at $x=e$ is
$f(e)=\frac{e}{\log e}=e$
